cases.name: (h) THE OWNER'S DECISION: the operator (not an agent) ratifies or vetoes only a motion the count gated to them, once, with `owner` keyed on every view
cases.vector: POST /api/v0/motions/{id}/decide over the fleet lab: the endpoint probe (m0 -> 404 `no motion with id m0`); `owner` keyed-null on every fresh view; 400 approve missing/non-boolean, note empty/blank/over 1000; 404 unknown id; 405 GET; 409 naming the state for an `open`, a `carried` (ungated — a majority is never routed around) and a `rejected` motion; FOUR decisions (tie -> ratified with a note, a second tie -> vetoed with none, two awaiting_owner carries -> ratified and vetoed) with the note byte-exact in the decide response, the single-motion GET and the collection view, and `null` in both when absent; the body's authority is the operator's (an `agent_cid`, here the unseated builder's, is ignored BY DESIGN — no agent lookup; see the case note); the tally and the four votes survive the decision; a decided motion takes no further vote (409 naming ratified and vetoed) and is decided once (409); and the SSE frame stays exactly {id,kind,state} carrying ratified AND vetoed with no text

notes: the IGNORED `agent_cid` above is INTENDED behaviour, not a gap (the SUT author's own reasoning, recorded so a later reader does not 'fix' it): the owner is the operator, so no agent identity is meaningful on this path — `DecideRequest` has no `agent_cid` field and `Council::decide` takes no `ConnectedAgent`, so there is nothing to look up; ignoring an extra key is the daemon-wide convention (`ProposeRequest` and `VoteRequest` carry no `deny_unknown_fields` either), and a caller that meant to act as an agent uses `/vote`, where `agent_cid` is required, typed and register-checked. A stray `agent_cid` on `/decide` grants nothing and changes nothing. If a future operator-identity slice (a real principal on the loopback edge) makes the principal explicit, `agent_cid` on `/decide` should become a 400 and this case must change with it: the invariant above pins today's intended behaviour, not a defect.
